exposure: Obstetricians' cognitive and affective traits (reflective coping, proactive coping, ambiguity tolerance, need for cognition, anxiety)
Obstetrician psychometric test scores by quartile
cohort: 94 obstetricians and 3488 of their nulliparous, term, cephalic, nonanomalous singleton deliveries
finding: Obstetricians with higher reflective coping scores were less likely to perform operative vaginal delivery, while lower anxiety and higher ambiguity tolerance were associated with increased risk of chorioamnionitis and postpartum hemorrhage, respectively.
mod_finding: Physicians with the most reflective coping were significantly less likely to perform operative vaginal delivery.
